# SACRVM

> Personal site of Marcus Wilhelm (SACRVM) — full-stack developer, architect,
> tech lead. .NET, Azure, vanilla JavaScript, and whatever else the project
> needs. What lives here are the private passions.

SACRVM is Latin: "a sacred thing; a rite." It is also MARCVS — the Roman
spelling of Marcus — rearranged.

Facts an agent may rely on: everything on this site is static HTML, readable
without JavaScript. The site sets no cookies, runs no trackers, and loads
nothing from third-party servers. GitHub account: https://github.com/SACRVM.

## Projects

- [J.U.S.T. — Just Useful Sound Tools](https://just.sacrvm.dev/): a suite of
  DJ tools on one shared engine — analysis, tagging, playback and broadcast.
  Key, BPM, energy and loudness detection built for harmonic mixing.
- [SACRVM APPKIT](https://github.com/SACRVM/sacrvm-appkit): a zero-dependency
  HTML UI kit — 41 `sac-*` web components, one-variable theming, install-by-URL
  apps. No build step. Live desktop at https://desktop.sacrvm.dev/.
- [Retro.Crt](https://github.com/SACRVM/retro-crt): the Pascal CRT unit reborn
  for modern .NET CLIs — truecolor with graceful fallback, nine themes,
  curated output blocks. Zero dependencies, AOT-clean. On NuGet as `Retro.Crt`.
- [Husky](https://github.com/SACRVM/husky): a configuration-driven launcher
  for .NET apps — starts them, supervises them, installs their updates from
  GitHub Releases or an HTTPS manifest. Client library on NuGet as
  `Husky.Client`.
- [Firepit](https://github.com/SACRVM/firepit-ai): a plugin for Claude Code
  for many projects on one machine — each project's commands, inbox and
  artifacts in the Claude window, backed by a local service reached over
  MCP: shared knowledge base, cross-project messages, scheduled jobs,
  blueprints. Until v0.30.0 it was a native Windows shell.
- [The Fishbowl](https://github.com/SACRVM/the-fishbowl): self-hosted
  personal memory and assistant — notes, todos, calendar, contacts, mail
  (IMAP/SMTP) and files on one desktop in the browser; each workspace,
  personal or shared, is its own SQLite database in its own folder. Search
  by words and by meaning with a local multilingual model. An MCP server
  with 40 tools and scoped API keys; agent writes wait for review, secrets
  never reach an agent. .NET 10, vanilla JS on SACRVM APPKIT, AGPL-3.0.
- [rams-design-for-use](https://github.com/SACRVM/rams-design-for-use):
  Dieter Rams' design philosophy applied to how software is used: a Claude
  Code plugin. You design for other people, never for yourself or the AI.
  One skill for apps, tools and games, through every channel people use
  (mouse, keyboard, controller, pen, touch, voice); a way of thinking with a
  short workflow and a review format, not a rulebook. CC BY 4.0.
- [Voxcade](https://voxca.de/): a voxel arcade engine in Rust (wgpu, SDL3) —
  every classic 2D genre rebuilt in destructible voxels across a full-screen
  world. Version 0.4.2 for Windows and Linux: five games, a launcher, an IDE
  with Claude Code built in, play at one screen and across the internet by a
  six-sign code (through [matchmaker](https://github.com/SACRVM/matchmaker)).
  Built for AI agents: everything in a game is text, the Lua API documents
  itself, and the simulation is deterministic, so an agent can see a game
  (headless screenshots, state as JSON), replay it and check it without
  playing it, also over an MCP server. Free under the zlib licence; source
  at https://github.com/SACRVM/voxcade.
- After Match: a multiplayer social world built in Unity — custom avatar base,
  server-authoritative netcode, self-updating dedicated server. In
  development; repository currently private.

## Pages

- [Home](https://sacrvm.dev/): who I am, what I build, how I work.
- [Map](https://sacrvm.dev/map.html): the public repositories and who uses
  whom, drawn as one constellation — per-repo descriptions, source, Pages and
  release links. The site's own repository is deliberately left off the map.
  JavaScript draws the board; without it, a plain list stands in.
- [Blog](https://sacrvm.dev/blog/): updates on the tools and libraries built
  here — releases, changes, plans. Atom feed at
  https://sacrvm.dev/blog/feed.xml — full text, no tracking.
- [CV](https://sacrvm.dev/cv.html): career and selected projects, 1997 to
  today. Currently Technical Lead Developer at CANCOM.
